subject: RE: BrightBay redlines — availability targets, credits, and maintenance cadence
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@brightbay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbay.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: BrightBay redlines: MSA + Order Form (availability/credits/questions)

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached are BrightBay's redlines to the MSA and Order Form. High-level asks from Legal/Procurement:

- Availability: target 99.95% monthly uptime for the Production model endpoint.
- Service credits: tiered credits starting at 5% for <99.95, up to 50% for prolonged outages; no monetary cap referenced in our redline.
- Response times: P1 (service down) — 1 hour initial response, 4 hour remediation target; P2 — 4 hours initial response.
- Maintenance: only weekend windows, minimum 72 hours advance notice; no maintenance during peak billing week (first week of month).

Please confirm Redwood's position and attach any counter-redlines. We need to present legal's recommendation to finance by Friday.

Attachments: BrightBay_MSA_redline_20261011.pdf, OrderForm_BrightBay_v3.docx

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Sr. Counsel — BrightBay Logistics
claire.nguyen@brightbay.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@brightbay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBay redlines: MSA + Order Form (availability/credits/questions)

Claire —

Received, thank you for the redlines and the clear summary. We appreciate BrightBay's thoroughness. Quick reaction and proposed next steps below, followed by a suggested timeline. My goal here is to preserve availability guarantees while keeping commercial exposure manageable so we can move to signature next week.

Summary of Redwood positions (high level):
- Availability: we can commit to 99.9% monthly uptime for Production. The incremental operational cost to guarantee 99.95% across all endpoint topologies is material; 99.9% is the level our Dedicated customers take for similar workloads.
- Service credits: we propose a tiered credit schedule with a monthly cap equal to 30% of that month's recurring fee (not unlimited). Credits should be the exclusive remedy for availability failures.
- Response times: agree to tight SLAs for Severity 1 incidents but propose initial response = 30 minutes (phone/RT), remediation objective = 4 hours for P1 where feasible. For some cross-region failovers the remediation window can be longer; we will include clear definitions.
- Maintenance: we can accept weekend maintenance with 48 hours notice as standard and provide an option for BrightBay to opt into a predictable monthly maintenance window to reduce last-minute disruptions. We cannot commit to never scheduling maintenance during the first billing week, but will include an exception process for critical monthly reporting windows.

Suggested next steps:
1) Internal alignment: Legal + Sales + Account Exec (Marissa) to finalize Redwood counter-redline — CC'd.
2) Prepare a short one-page SLA summary to attach to the order form capturing uptime measurement method, credit calculation, and incident classification.
3) Schedule a 30-minute sync with BrightBay Legal & Procurement — propose Tue Oct 13 at 10:00 AM PT.

I am attaching a draft counter-redline PDF (Redwood_Counterredline_MSA_20261012.pdf) that reflects the above; legal will refine language but wanted to share our commercial posture.

If you prefer, we can also present an optional managed tier (higher availability) with a price uplift and a 99.95% target — happy to detail that on the call.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

--Attached: Redwood_Counterredline_MSA_20261012.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBay redlines: MSA + Order Form (availability/credits/questions)

Eve/Marissa —

Thanks — commercial thoughts:
- If BrightBay insists on 99.95 as standard, we should present a priced upgrade. Let's not concede 99.95 in the MSA without commercial compensation.
- Credit cap: 30% monthly cap is OK as a starting point, but can we get to 25% if we define measurement windows (rolling 30-day) and exclude scheduled maintenance/force majeure?
- For response times, 30-minute initial response for P1 is reasonable operationally (we have on-call), but remediation "target" language should be objective-based, not a hard SLA for events requiring third-party cloud provider fixes.

Ask: Marissa, can we run the counter-redline through finance for modeling? If finance flags commercial risk, we will escalate to Sales Ops.

Also, I suggest we prepare two order-form variants: Standard (99.9%, lower fee) and Premium (99.95%, price uplift + defined deployment footprint). That should unblock procurement quickly.

Karthik
Senior Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightBay redlines: legal comments on availability language

Team —

I reviewed BrightBay's redlines and Evelyn's draft counter. A few legal drafting notes to avoid open-ended liability and ambiguous measurement:

1) Definitions: clearly define "Available" vs "Degraded" vs "Unavailable". Credits should only apply to "Unavailable" as measured by successful end-to-end request success rate to the production endpoint (we should specify measurement agent and aggregation).
2) Measurement window: use rolling 30-day window and define minimum sample size for measurement so a single short blip doesn't trigger large credits.
3) Cap & Exclusive Remedy: maintain a financial cap (25-30%) and add explicit language that credits are the exclusive remedy for availability failures; exclude consequential damages.
4) Exceptions: scheduled maintenance (with notice), customer-caused incidents, network outages outside Redwood's control, and force majeure should be explicit carve-outs.
5) Escalation & Credits workflow: include a 14-day root cause analysis process before credits are automatically applied; allow customer to request expedited RCA where necessary.

I'll draft concrete language and attach redline snippets for Marissa to incorporate. If we go with the two-tiered approach (Standard vs Premium), legal should also add wording for what constitutes the Premium deployment topology to avoid ambiguity.

-Olga
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@brightbay.com>, procurement@brightbay.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightBay redlines: MSA + Order Form (availability/credits/questions)

Claire —

Thanks for the redlines and for the clear timeline. Attached is Redwood's consolidated counter-redline (Redwood_Counterredline_MSA_20261012.pdf) plus a one-page SLA summary that highlights: uptime target options, how uptime is measured, our proposed credit tiers (with a monthly cap), incident severity definitions, and a scheduled maintenance flow.

To summarize our commercial posture and next steps:
- We can offer a Standard production SLA at 99.9% with the attached credit schedule (monthly cap 30%).
- We will provide a Premium SLA at 99.95% for customers who opt into a priced deployment footprint (details in the one-pager).
- We propose a 30-minute initial response for P1 incidents and objective-based remediation targets; legal will include carve-outs for cloud-provider incidents.
- Maintenance: 48 hours standard notice; BrightBay can request blackout dates via the change management process and we will treat a limited set of dates as higher-avoidance windows where possible.

Would BrightBay be available for a 30-minute call Tue Oct 13 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the counter and agree on a final path? If that time doesn't work, please propose two alternatives.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

--Attachments: Redwood_Counterredline_MSA_20261012.pdf; SLA_one-pager_BrightBay_20261012.pdf
